findings.evidence: features/002-develop-skill/002-develop-skill-prd.md:R5 + AC-8 — R5 says 'The Gate 4 manifest's reviewer set may flag a `block` finding naming the lane assignment as too aggressive (e.g. blast radius judged Low when the plan reveals a multi-module change). When such a finding lands and is accepted in Round 2, the plan must be re-emitted with the corrected lane and Gate 4 must re-fire before code is written.' AC-8 enforces this: 'When a Gate 4 round-1 finding has severity `block` AND the finding's `claim` field references the lane assignment as too aggressive AND the AI accepts in round-2, the Gate 4 manifest's closing decision records the re-lane.' The trigger condition relies on a string-match against the finding's `claim` field ('references the lane assignment as too aggressive') — but no reviewer in the standard five has lane-checking in their explicit lens, and no `claim` shape is documented for what 'references the lane assignment' means. Reviewers will under-fire (a too-aggressive lane goes unflagged because no reviewer's lens covers it) OR a string-match implementation will over-fire (any `claim` mentioning 'lane' triggers a re-lane, including findings that aren't about lane aggressiveness). The PRD commits to the lane-recheck mechanism without naming the load-bearing assumption that one of the five reviewers will reliably catch lane misjudgements.
findings.claim: Missing tradeoff articulation + unstated assumption — R5 + AC-8's lane-recheck mechanism assumes 'one of the standard five reviewers will reliably flag a too-aggressive lane assignment as a `block` finding,' but neither the PRD nor the reviewer role definitions in `templates/agents/standard/principles/*.md` document lane-checking as part of any reviewer's lens. The Goal-Driven Reviewer reviews coverage; Surgical reviews trace integrity; Think-Before-Coding reviews unstated assumptions; Simplicity reviews speculative complexity; Devil's Advocate reviews cross-artefact ambiguity. None of these natively own 'verifiability or blast-radius score is too low'. Without an explicit lane-recheck lens assigned to a reviewer (or a separate lane-recheck step before Gate 4), AC-8 is non-firing in practice — the reviewer fleet doesn't have the responsibility to fire what AC-8 enforces.
findings.proposed_change: Either (a) add an explicit pre-Gate-4 lane-recheck step as a separate requirement, with a structured check (`re-evaluate the four-axis tuple given the plan's actual file list; downgrade if the plan reveals more files than the task scope claimed`) that runs before Gate 4 reviewers fire — making the lane-recheck mechanical, not reviewer-judgement-dependent; OR (b) extend the role definition of the Goal-Driven Reviewer to explicitly include lane-recheck as a Gate-4 lens (e.g. 'at Gate 4, Goal-Driven Reviewer verifies that the plan's file list does not contradict the lane assignment's blast-radius cited evidence'), and update R10 + AC-8 to name Goal-Driven as the load-bearing reviewer for lane-recheck. Option (a) is more reliable (mechanical check beats reviewer judgement on this); option (b) preserves the reviewer-pattern. Either resolves the unstated assumption.

findings.evidence: features/002-develop-skill/002-develop-skill-prd.md:R12 — 'When Codex is absent, the standard five-reviewer set runs Gate 5 with Goal-Driven Reviewer load-bearing (code-vs-plan acceptance is its lens) and Devil's Advocate covering cross-provider concerns DA can spot in same-provider review.' The phrase 'cross-provider concerns DA can spot in same-provider review' is internally contradictory — if DA is running in the same provider as the writer, by definition it cannot fully cover cross-provider concerns (that's why Codex is the load-bearing reviewer when present). The PRD names the degraded-coverage manifest note (good) but R12's rationale paragraph implies DA fills the cross-provider gap, which it cannot. A reader interpreting R12 may think DA-as-Codex-substitute is sufficient when the manifest note is the truthful framing.
findings.claim: Single-interpretation framing of an ambiguous degraded path — R12 frames Devil's Advocate as 'covering cross-provider concerns' when in same-provider review DA cannot do that. The accurate framing is the manifest note R12 already specifies ('Cross-provider findings may be missed; install Codex CLI for full Gate 5 coverage'), not the rationale claim. Reviewers reading R12 should not be left with the impression that the absent-Codex path has full coverage.
findings.proposed_change: Edit R12's rationale to remove the 'DA covers cross-provider concerns' phrasing and replace with: 'When Codex is absent, the standard five-reviewer set runs Gate 5 with Goal-Driven Reviewer load-bearing (code-vs-plan acceptance is its lens). Devil's Advocate runs as part of the standard set, but cross-provider review is not available — the manifest note (below) is the authoritative framing of degraded coverage.' This keeps DA in the reviewer set as documented but stops the rationale from over-claiming what same-provider review can do.
